correctness.rationale: The verifier reconstructs the 16-vertex, 48-edge Cayley graph; the exact face vector (16,72,96,16); boundary ranks 57 and 16; and 16 unit Smith factors for the third boundary, establishing free integral H2 of rank 23. A flag support lemma restricts six-vertex carriers to octahedra, and all 8008 six-subsets are checked, yielding 32. All oct cycles have zero signed boundary, and 192 explicit affine automorphisms act transitively. The 96-by-48 matrix formed from third boundaries and oct cycles has 38 unit Smith factors and one factor 2, proving index two in the full cycle lattice. A complete 11440-case seven-vertex binary homology census yields 320 single-octahedron carriers and 11120 zero cases; mod-two detection in the index-two quotient excludes integral coset classes on at most seven vertices. The stated eight-vertex induced complex collapses by two checked free-face pairs onto a sphere with face vector (8,18,12); the signed 12-triangle cycle has zero boundary, and adjoining it produces 39 unit Smith factors. Every computational assertion is recreated from the included program, not from prior-run logs.

This is a bounded originality assessment, not an absolute priority certificate.

value.rationale: This is a naturally motivated integral local-to-global question for a canonical exceptional strongly regular graph. Exactly 32 smallest sphere cycles give the full rational homology but a proper index-two integer lattice, a distinction invisible from known wedge homotopy and symmetry characters. An explicit eight-vertex spherical cycle repairs the missing coset, while a full seven-vertex census establishes that the extra support is sharp. The obstruction provides a concrete boundary to the assumption that minimal induced homology spheres generate integrally; it is not merely a repeated Betti calculation or a small arbitrary parameter change.
